label: Myth, Break, Model
line: State the belief the viewer holds in its strongest form, break it in one line, then build the right model on a case the viewer is living through right now.
best_for: a belief most people hold is wrong
advice or a habit that rests on an outdated idea, with a real study or figure as the proof
also_for: practical advice, told as the belief it corrects
avoid_for: a trivia correction with no mechanism behind it
a myth already debunked everywhere: the debunk is the part people know

beats.name: The belief
beats.job: As the viewer learned it, or as a warning in the viewer's own words.

beats.name: The break
beats.job: One line: that is wrong, or that stopped being true.

beats.name: Case A
beats.job: Where the old belief seems to hold, and what is really happening there.

beats.name: Case B
beats.job: Where it fails. One real named source, study or number.

beats.name: Tie to the viewer
beats.job: The thing the viewer is doing right now is case B. Or the viewer's objection, spoken.

beats.name: Second sting or action
beats.job: A related well-known 'fact' that is also wrong, or the one thing to do.

hooks.shape: You were taught [belief]. That is wrong.
[Thing everybody does to stay safe or healthy] does nothing for [what it is meant to protect].
If [belief] were true, why does [everyday counter-example] happen?

holds: The belief is the viewer's own, so the answer has to overturn something they hold. A pair of contrasting cases carries the middle. The viewer's objection, spoken at about three fifths, re-opens the question.
ending: The precise statement, then a second sting or one concrete action. No moral.
pitfalls: Confirming the myth at length before breaking it
A hedge where the verdict belongs
An invented study: the source must be real and named
template: You were taught [belief]. That is wrong. When [case A], [what really happens]. But [case B] breaks it: [real named fact or study]. [The thing you are doing right now] is [case B]. So the truth is [precise statement]. And [a related well-known fact] is wrong too.
